### Cassville

- **Type:** Town
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** April 16, 2026 (town electors voted 44-0 that evening to authorize the Town Board to exercise village powers/zoning authority, and the Board adopted the data center ban ordinance the same evening)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-04-16` (exact)
- **Duration:** Up to two years
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `wi-cassville-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Town of Cassville (Grant County) data center ban ordinance, adopted using newly authorized village/zoning powers (ordinance number not located in reviewed sources)
- **What prompted it:** A proposed roughly $1 billion, approximately 500-acre data center campus by an undisclosed developer (drawn by the town's proximity to the Cardinal-Hickory Creek high-voltage transmission line); residents opposed the secrecy and scale of the project and mobilized to give the town board zoning authority to block it.
- **Affected projects:** An anonymous developer's proposed ~$1 billion, 400-500 megawatt data center campus (roughly 500 acres) near the Cardinal-Hickory Creek transmission line; the developer reportedly went quiet after the town's action and was also considering sites in Indiana and North Dakota.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; enacted April 16, 2026. Prohibits data centers in the town for up to two years and also restricts land-use changes (e.g., building a residence on farmland) without town board approval. The county cannot preempt the town's zoning authority in this instance. As of the reporting reviewed, the previously scouted developer had gone quiet, with no application filed.
- **Outcome:** Town electors authorized village/zoning powers and the Town Board adopted a two-year ban on data centers, blocking the proposed project.

### Manitowoc County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-04-28
- **Normalized date:** `2026-04-28` (exact)
- **Duration:** 18 months from the date the ordinance is published (its effective date), or until the County Board adopts and the County Executive approves amendments, or rescinds the moratorium, whichever occurs first
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `wi-manitowoc-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance 2026/2028-10, creating Manitowoc County Code Sec. 8.495
- **What prompted it:** Town petitions from Mishicot, Two Creeks, and Two Rivers; concerns about health and safety, air quality, water resources, water use, electricity demand, fire hazards, public services, roads, property values, noise, visual impacts, farmland preservation, and lack of county data center standards.
- **Affected projects:** Data centers in county-zoned areas, especially Mishicot, Two Creeks, and Two Rivers. Reporting identifies Cloverleaf Infrastructure land outreach in the area, but no filed project application was identified.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. Confirmed directly against the final adopted ordinance text (No. 2026/2028-10, county code Sec. 8.495): an earlier planning-commission draft (2026-PZ-9A4, 04/27/2026) specified 12 months, but WPR and the final adopted text (2026-PZ-9A6, dated 04/29/2026, published by the Town of Two Rivers as "adopted by the Manitowoc County Board 4-28-2026") confirm the County Board amended the term from 12 to 18 months on the floor before final passage. The 18-month term (from publication ~April 28-29, 2026, running to approximately late October 2027) had not lapsed as of 2026-09-23, and no repeal, rescission, or amendment was found in subsequent county records or news coverage.
- **Outcome:** Pending. The county plans to study impacts and develop zoning and regulatory standards.

### Marathon County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** August 25, 2026 (County Board approval)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-25` (exact)
- **Duration:** At least 12 months
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `wi-marathon-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Marathon County zoning code amendment (ordinance) enacting a data center moratorium, citing Wis. Stat. § 59.02 and § 59.69 (ordinance number not located in reviewed sources)
- **What prompted it:** High electrical demand, utility infrastructure requirements, cooling/mechanical systems, noise, emergency power generation, and land-use compatibility concerns associated with data center development; 7 of 18 affected townships responded to a staff survey in support before passage.
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; approved August 25, 2026, applying to the 18 townships governed by county zoning (Brighton, Easton, Eau Pleine, Elderon, Frankfort, Green Valley, Guenther, Hewitt, Holton, Hull, Knowlton, Marathon, McMillan, Reid, Rib Falls, Plover, Spencer, and Wien). Applies to proposed facilities where data center operation is a primary use and cumulative gross floor area exceeds 5,000 square feet; exempts previously issued approvals, ordinary maintenance, and emergency utility restoration. Staff must report progress to the Environmental Resources Committee six months after passage.
- **Outcome:** Adopted at-least-12-month moratorium on data center-related zoning approvals in the 18 county-zoned townships.

### Milwaukee

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟡 Pending
- **Date enacted:** —
- **Normalized date:** `—` (unverified)
- **Duration:** Proposed one year
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `wi-milwaukee-undated`
- **Legal basis:** Proposed Milwaukee Common Council ordinance imposing a one-year data center moratorium, sponsored by Alderwoman Marina Dimitrijevic with Alex Brower, Russell W. Stamper II, and Robert Bauman; endorsed by the Zoning Code Technical Committee August 10, 2026
- **What prompted it:** Milwaukee's zoning code does not currently treat data centers as a distinct land use; sponsor wants rules in place before a major data center proposal is submitted, following controversy over a since-withdrawn data center component of a Midtown Center Walmart-site redevelopment.
- **Affected projects:** A 19,000-square-foot "computer research facility" that opponents characterized as a data center was initially part of a proposed Midtown Center (former Walmart site) redevelopment; the developer later removed it from the plan.
- **Detailed status:** Pending as of 2026-09-23. The City Plan Commission is scheduled to hold its hearing and make a recommendation on September 28, 2026; the proposal still requires Common Council approval before taking effect. If adopted, the moratorium would bar city departments/boards/commissions from accepting or processing most new data center applications for one year after passage or until the zoning code is amended to specifically regulate data centers, whichever is first, with an exception for planned-development-district properties and a proposed (contested) tribal-land exemption for the Forest County Potawatomi Community.
- **Outcome:** Zoning Code Technical Committee endorsed the proposed one-year data center moratorium (Aug. 10, 2026); City Plan Commission hearing scheduled Sept. 28, 2026; Common Council vote still required.

As drafted, the moratorium would freeze acceptance, review, or approval of development permits for data centers, BESS, and solar energy systems exceeding one acre, for 12 months, with exemptions for solar installations of one acre or less, ordinary maintenance/repairs, emergency utility restoration, and projects already holding valid county permits.

### Village of Wrightstown

- **Type:** Village

This followed a separate, earlier June 16, 2026 action in which the Board voted 6-0 to impose a shorter, interim pause on data-center zoning and planning activity specifically until the August 11, 2026 advisory referendum was certified; the July 7 ordinance extended that interim pause into a full one-year moratorium.

- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center

- **What prompted it:** Adopted following a resident petition, while an August 11, 2026 advisory referendum on municipal utility/infrastructure commitments for a large-scale data center project remained scheduled.
- **Affected projects:** Large-scale data center project that is the subject of the scheduled August 11, 2026 advisory referendum.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. The Village Board adopted a one-year moratorium on all zoning and planning activities related to data centers on July 7, 2026 (6-0), extending a shorter interim pause the Board had adopted June 16, 2026 pending the outcome of an August 11, 2026 advisory referendum. That referendum was held as scheduled and was defeated: of 1,184 votes cast, 87.25% (1,033) voted "No" on whether the Village should authorize, support, or facilitate public resources or infrastructure for a large-scale data center development (a non-binding result that does not itself alter the moratorium). No repeal, rescission, or replacement of the July 7 moratorium ordinance was found as of 2026-09-23. - **Outcome:** Adopted one-year moratorium on data center projects.
